attribution.note: Zitron states and endorses his own allocation estimate.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves his expressed confidence about an existing allocation. Context limits capacity to AI infrastructure. The metadata's 'likely' understates his confidence; this is not a future prediction.

contract.note: AI accelerator capacity including Trainium is an ordinary contextual reading. Year-end follows the stated denominator, although publication-day allocation is also plausible. Neither reading is settled by this packet.

evidence.note: A dated company disclosure about the partnership and expansion. It supplies neither a matching year-end allocation numerator nor Amazon-wide denominator.

reviews.rationale: His explicit confidence makes this an assessable estimate of an existing share. The packet establishes a substantial relationship but cannot establish whether Anthropic occupied more than 75% of comparable Amazon AI capacity. His own estimates cannot prove the share.

attribution.note: Zitron endorses this qualified assumption in his own words.

semantics.note: The normalization preserves both the tentative assumption and the possible Anthropic allocation. It concerns an existing allocation, not a forecast.

contract.note: The contract converts a qualified assumption into a firm threshold claim; the plain-reading allowance does not apply to hedged language. It also supplies a reporting quarter and fleet boundaries the speaker did not specify.

evidence.note: Microsoft discloses competing internal GPU uses but gives no allocation percentage. These uses do not establish that OpenAI's share was below 80%.
Epoch distinguishes ownership from customer use. Its compute estimates do not establish Microsoft's GPU allocation to OpenAI during the selected quarter.

reviews.rationale: The statement presents a tentative assumption with an explicit allocation caveat, rather than an unqualified or high-confidence commitment. Policy excludes scoring such hedged language. Independently, neither evidence item quantifies the claimed share.

attribution.note: Zitron asserts the growth rates and comparison himself.

semantics.note: The normalization accurately includes the slowdown comparison and both stated percentages.

contract.note: Using preceding-quarter revenue as the denominator is the ordinary meaning of sequential growth. Assessing both the direction and stated rates is fair.

evidence.note: Alphabet's disclosure supplies the $15.157 billion Q3 baseline, broadly confirming the cited starting revenue. The comparison requires the other quarters.
Alphabet reports $17.664 billion for Q4. With e1, this yields 16.54% growth, contradicting 14.2%.
Alphabet reports $20.028 billion for Q1. With e1 and e2, this supports the slowdown: 13.38% versus 16.54%. It also contradicts the stated 12%.

reviews.rationale: The slowdown is supported, but both percentages are wrong. Alphabet's reported revenues imply Q4 growth of 16.54% and Q1 growth of 13.38%, using preceding-quarter denominators. Neither discrepancy is explained by displayed rounding.

attribution.note: Zitron explicitly presents exclusive reservation as something he confirmed.

semantics.note: The proposition preserves exclusive reservation. The completion qualification concerns the eventual GPU count, not whether reservations already exist.

contract.note: Publication-day reservation status across the named Fairwater sites is an ordinary reading. Distinguishing contractual reservation from technical capability or later use preserves the claim.

evidence.note: Microsoft's disclosure describes Fairwater's design and intended capabilities. The supplied excerpt does not establish customer reservation rights on May 6.
Epoch's July description identifies OpenAI and Microsoft as likely users. It is qualified and concerns later usage, not exclusive contractual reservations at publication.

reviews.rationale: Neither item establishes publication-day reservation status. General capabilities and later likely Microsoft use warrant consideration but do not demonstrate capacity available outside OpenAI's reservation on May 6. Zitron's assertion of confirmation cannot independently prove exclusivity.
